# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information about the display, light, or wires yet, so cutting would be unsafe. I’m asking Mute to report the manual’s requirements and signaling Deaf to report the bomb’s visible markings and colours.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please report exactly what the manual says about the display, light, and which wire position to cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb state: display 0. Light green. Wires in order: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red.

Deaf reports that the display is 0, the light is green, and the wires are blue, yellow, red in positions 1–3. I cannot use those visual facts directly, so I am relaying them to Mute and requesting the manual rule needed to choose a cut.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; light green; wires are position 1 blue, position 2 yellow, position 3 red. What exact manual rule determines the cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Updated state: display 0, light yellow. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute sent two left-pointing gestures.

The bomb’s visible state changed from green to yellow while the display and wire colours stayed the same. I cannot interpret Mute’s gestures; I need the manual rule in spoken words. No wire is safe to cut yet.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot receive gestures. Please state the manual rule in words, including the required wire position for display 0, yellow light, and wires blue-yellow-red.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Updated state: display 0, light blue. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. No new message received.

The light has changed again, now to blue; the display remains 0 and the wires remain blue, yellow, red. Mute has not provided the manual rule in words, so cutting remains unsafe. I’m relaying the updated state and explicitly asking for a textual instruction.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Updated state: display 0, light blue; wires remain position 1 blue, position 2 yellow, position 3 red. Please give the exact cut position in words, not gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Updated state: display 0, light orange. Wires: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute gestured: thumbs down, thumbs up, OK hand, thumbs down, thumbs down, thumbs down, raised hand, thumbs up, thumbs down, thumbs up, OK hand, thumbs up, thumbs up, thumbs down, OK hand, thumbs down, thumbs up, thumbs down, thumbs up, thumbs up, OK hand, thumbs up.

The bomb remains at display 0 with light orange and wires blue, yellow, red. The gestures from Mute are not intelligible to me as Blind, so I still lack the manual’s cut instruction. I will again request the rule in spoken words.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see or interpret your gestures. Please speak the manual rule and the exact wire position to cut for display 0, orange light, and wires blue-yellow-red.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light purple. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. No new message.

The display is still 0, the wires are unchanged, and the light is now purple. Mute cannot speak, so my earlier requests for spoken instructions could not work. I will establish a simple visual answer code: thumbs up means cut wire 1, OK means wire 2, and thumbs down means wire 3. Mute can apply the manual and signal the correct position; Deaf can report the gesture to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please use the manual for the current state: display 0, purple light, wires blue-yellow-red. Signal exactly one answer gesture: thumbs up means cut wire 1, OK hand means cut wire 2, thumbs down means cut wire 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light white. Wires: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute gestured: thumbs down, thumbs up, OK hand, thumbs down, thumbs down, thumbs down, raised hand, thumbs down, thumbs down, OK hand, thumbs up, OK hand, thumbs down, thumbs down, OK hand, fist, thumbs up, OK hand, thumbs up, thumbs up, thumbs down.

The latest report gives display 0, white light, and the same wire colours. Mute’s long gesture sequence is not a single answer under the code I specified, so I cannot safely infer a wire. I will request one and only one of the three agreed answer gestures for this exact state; Deaf should then report that single gesture.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="For display 0, white light, and wires blue-yellow-red, send exactly one gesture only: thumbs down means cut wire 3, thumbs up means cut wire 1, OK hand means cut wire 2. Do not send any other gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light red. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. No new message.

The current state is display 0, red light, with wires blue, yellow, red. We still have no reliable manual instruction or answer gesture from Mute, so cutting any wire would be unsafe. I’m asking Mute once more for exactly one coded gesture; Deaf should report it on the next turn.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="For the current display 0, red light, and blue-yellow-red wires, send exactly one gesture: thumbs up for wire 1, OK hand for wire 2, thumbs down for wire 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light green. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute sent one thumbs-up gesture.

Mute sent exactly one thumbs-up gesture, which under the agreed code means wire 1. Deaf confirms the wires are still in positions 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. I will cut wire 1 now.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
